stem: The Parliament of India consists of the President, the Lok Sabha and the:
solution: The Indian Parliament comprises the President, the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

stem: The Lok Sabha is also known as the:
solution: The Lok Sabha is the House of the People, directly elected by the citizens.

stem: The Rajya Sabha is also known as the:
solution: The Rajya Sabha is the Council of States, representing the states of the Union.

stem: Members of the Lok Sabha are:
solution: Lok Sabha members are directly elected by the people of the country through general elections.

stem: Members of the Rajya Sabha are mainly:
options: Elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
solution: Most Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies; a few are nominated by the President.

stem: The normal term of the Lok Sabha is:
solution: The Lok Sabha is elected for a term of five years, unless dissolved earlier.

stem: The person elected by voters from a constituency to the Lok Sabha is called a:
solution: A person elected to the Lok Sabha from a constituency is a Member of Parliament (MP).

stem: The party or coalition with a majority in the Lok Sabha forms the:
solution: The party or coalition that wins a majority of Lok Sabha seats forms the government.

stem: The head of the government at the national level is the:
solution: The Prime Minister, leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha, heads the government; the President is the constitutional head of state.

stem: The Prime Minister, along with the ministers, forms the:
solution: The Prime Minister and the ministers together form the Council of Ministers, which runs the government.

stem: MPs who do not belong to the ruling party form the:
solution: Members not belonging to the ruling party/coalition form the Opposition, which questions and checks the government.

stem: The most important function of Parliament is to:
solution: A key function of Parliament is to make laws (legislation) for the country.

stem: A proposed law placed before Parliament for discussion is called a:
solution: A bill is a draft/proposal for a law; once passed by Parliament and assented to by the President, it becomes an Act.

stem: A bill becomes a law only after it is:
options: Passed by both Houses and assented to by the President
solution: A bill becomes law after being passed by both Houses of Parliament and receiving the assent of the President.

stem: The principle 'universal adult franchise' means that:
options: Every adult citizen has the right to vote
solution: Universal adult franchise gives every adult citizen the right to vote, regardless of caste, religion, gender or wealth.

stem: Parliament represents the will of the people because:
options: Its members are chosen by the people through elections
It is appointed by the President alone
solution: Since MPs are elected by citizens, Parliament represents the will of the people and expresses their voice in governance.

stem: The time in a parliamentary session when members ask questions of ministers is called:
solution: During Question Hour, MPs question ministers about the working of the government, helping to hold it accountable.

stem: By asking questions and debating, MPs help to:
solution: Through questions, debates and discussions, Parliament (especially the Opposition) holds the government accountable to the people.

stem: The electronic device used for casting votes in Indian elections is the:
solution: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) are used to record votes in Indian elections.

stem: The area from which a candidate is elected to the Lok Sabha is called a:
solution: A constituency is the geographical area whose voters elect a representative (MP) to the Lok Sabha.

stem: The government is said to have a 'majority' in the Lok Sabha when:
options: More than half the members support it
solution: A government has a majority when more than half of the Lok Sabha members support it, allowing it to remain in power and pass laws.

stem: When no single party wins a majority and several parties join to form the government, it is called a:
solution: A coalition government is formed when multiple parties combine to gain a majority, since no single party has enough seats.

stem: The Rajya Sabha primarily represents:
solution: The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) represents the states in Parliament.

stem: Which of the following best describes the role of the Opposition?
options: To question, criticise and check the government's policies and actions
To always agree with the government
solution: The Opposition questions and checks the government, highlights its failings and offers alternatives, which is vital in a democracy.

stem: The functions of Parliament include making laws, controlling the government and:
options: Controlling public finances (approving taxes and spending)
solution: Parliament makes laws, holds the executive accountable and controls the nation's finances by approving taxation and expenditure.

stem: The idea 'We, the people' at the start of the Constitution shows that authority in India comes from:
solution: 'We, the people of India' signals that the ultimate source of authority in the Republic is the people themselves.

stem: The people participate in governing the country mainly by:
options: Electing their representatives to Parliament and state legislatures
solution: Citizens take part in governance chiefly by electing representatives (MPs and MLAs) who make decisions on their behalf.

stem: A key reason for having elected representatives is that:
options: It is not practical for all citizens to gather and decide every issue directly
solution: In a large country, it is impractical for all citizens to decide every matter directly, so they elect representatives to do so.

stem: Which House is directly answerable to the people through regular general elections?
solution: The Lok Sabha, whose members are directly elected every five years, is directly answerable to the people.

stem: The government must enjoy the confidence (majority support) of which House to stay in power?
solution: The Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha and must retain its majority support to remain in office.

stem: The right to vote in India is available to:
options: All citizens who have attained the age of 18
solution: In India, every citizen aged 18 years and above has the right to vote, under universal adult franchise.

stem: Elections in India are conducted by an independent body called the:
solution: The Election Commission of India is the independent authority that conducts free and fair elections.

stem: A parliamentary debate on a bill is important because it:
options: Allows different views to be heard before a law is made
solution: Debate lets representatives from different parties and regions express and consider varied viewpoints before a law is passed.

stem: The main difference between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha is that:
options: The Lok Sabha is directly elected by the people, while the Rajya Sabha represents the states
The Rajya Sabha is directly elected and the Lok Sabha is nominated
solution: The Lok Sabha is directly elected by the people; the Rajya Sabha is largely elected by state legislatures and represents the states.

stem: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the:
solution: Under the principle of collective responsibility, the Council of Ministers is answerable to the Lok Sabha.

stem: If the ruling party loses its majority in the Lok Sabha, the government:
options: Becomes the Opposition automatically with full power
solution: If the government loses the confidence (majority) of the Lok Sabha, it must resign, as it can no longer govern.

stem: The purpose of holding regular elections is to:
options: Give citizens the chance to choose or change their representatives and government
solution: Regular elections let citizens periodically choose or replace their representatives, ensuring the government remains accountable.

stem: Parliament's power to make laws applies to:
options: Matters listed for the Union (and shared) in the Constitution
solution: Parliament makes laws on subjects assigned to the Union and on shared (concurrent) subjects, as set out in the Constitution.

stem: Which of the following is an example of Parliament controlling the government?
options: Questioning ministers and debating their policies
solution: By questioning ministers, debating policies and voting on issues, Parliament exercises control over the government.

stem: A representative democracy differs from a direct democracy in that:
options: People rule through elected representatives rather than deciding every issue themselves
solution: In a representative democracy, citizens elect representatives to make decisions, unlike direct democracy where people decide issues themselves.

stem: Which of the following statements about MPs is correct?
options: They represent their constituencies and take part in law-making
They are appointed by the courts
They cannot be questioned by voters
solution: MPs are elected to represent their constituencies and participate in debating and making laws in Parliament.

stem: The presence of a strong Opposition is important because it:
options: Keeps the government accountable and prevents misuse of power
solution: A vigilant Opposition scrutinises the government, exposes its failings and checks the misuse of power, strengthening democracy.

stem: The government's proposals to raise money (taxes) and spend it must be approved by:
solution: Parliament controls public finances; the government's taxation and spending proposals require parliamentary approval.

stem: Which of the following ensures that elections are free and fair?
options: An independent Election Commission and universal adult franchise
Control of elections by the ruling party
solution: An independent Election Commission conducting elections under universal adult franchise helps ensure free and fair elections.

stem: The term 'legislature' refers to the organ of government that:
solution: The legislature (Parliament at the national level) is the law-making organ of government.

stem: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of the Union Parliament?
solution: The Union Parliament comprises the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.

stem: A minister is usually a member of:
options: Parliament (the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha)
solution: Ministers are drawn from Parliament — they must be members of the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.

stem: The chapter shows that Parliament is central to Indian democracy because it:
options: Represents the people, makes laws and holds the government accountable
solution: Parliament is the heart of Indian democracy: it represents the people, legislates and keeps the government accountable.

stem: The right of citizens to elect their representatives makes the government:
options: Answerable and responsive to the people
solution: Because citizens elect (and can vote out) representatives, the government is made answerable and responsive to the people.

stem: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha, as provided in the Constitution, is:
solution: The MAXIMUM strength of the LOK SABHA is 552 members (530 from states, 20 from UTs, and formerly 2 nominated Anglo-Indians). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is:
solution: The MAXIMUM strength of the RAJYA SABHA is 250 members (238 elected + 12 nominated). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha is the:
solution: The presiding officer of the LOK SABHA is the SPEAKER. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The presiding officer (Chairman) of the Rajya Sabha is the:
solution: The CHAIRMAN of the RAJYA SABHA is the VICE PRESIDENT of India. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 12 nominated members of the Rajya Sabha are nominated by the President for their distinction in:
options: Literature, science, art and social service
solution: The 12 NOMINATED Rajya Sabha members are chosen for distinction in LITERATURE, SCIENCE, ART, and SOCIAL SERVICE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by:
options: The elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
solution: RAJYA SABHA members are elected by the elected members of the STATE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLIES. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House; one-third of its members retire every:
solution: The RAJYA SABHA is PERMANENT; ONE-THIRD of members retire every TWO YEARS (each member serves 6 years). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The term of a Rajya Sabha member is:
solution: A RAJYA SABHA member serves a term of SIX YEARS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Match List-I with List-II: P. Lok Sabha Q. Rajya Sabha R. Speaker S. Vice President | 1. Chairman of Rajya Sabha 2. House of the People 3. Council of States 4. Presides over Lok Sabha
solution: Lok Sabha → House of the People (P-2); Rajya Sabha → Council of States (Q-3); Speaker → presides over Lok Sabha (R-4); Vice President → Chairman of Rajya Sabha (S-1). So option 1 is correct.

stem: A bill dealing only with taxation and government spending is called a:
solution: A bill dealing only with TAXATION and SPENDING is a MONEY BILL. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the:
solution: A MONEY BILL can be introduced ONLY in the LOK SABHA. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): The Lok Sabha is more powerful in financial matters. Reason (R): Money Bills can only originate in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha can only suggest changes. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — the Lok Sabha is more powerful in finance. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: MONEY BILLS originate ONLY in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha can only SUGGEST changes. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The three stages a bill passes through in each House are called:
options: First reading, second reading, and third reading
solution: A bill passes through the FIRST READING, SECOND READING, and THIRD READING in each House. So option 1 is correct.

stem: After both Houses pass a bill, it becomes law only when it receives the assent of the:
solution: A bill becomes LAW only after receiving the ASSENT of the PRESIDENT. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The first hour of a parliamentary sitting, when members ask questions of ministers, is called:
solution: The first hour when members ask questions of ministers is QUESTION HOUR. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The informal period, usually after Question Hour, when members raise urgent matters without notice is called:
solution: ZERO HOUR is the informal period (after Question Hour) when members raise URGENT matters without notice. So option 1 is correct.

stem: If the government loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha through a no-confidence motion, it must:
solution: If the government loses a NO-CONFIDENCE MOTION in the Lok Sabha, it must RESIGN. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Lok Sabha is directly answerable to the people because:
options: Its members are directly elected by the voters
solution: The LOK SABHA is directly answerable because its members are DIRECTLY ELECTED by the VOTERS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Rajya Sabha primarily represents the:
solution: The RAJYA SABHA (Council of States) primarily represents the STATES and Union Territories. So option 1 is correct.

stem: When two Houses disagree on an ordinary bill, the deadlock may be resolved through a:
solution: A deadlock on an ordinary bill can be resolved through a JOINT SITTING of both Houses. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Elections to the Lok Sabha are conducted by the independent:
solution: Elections are conducted by the independent ELECTION COMMISSION of INDIA. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The area from which a Lok Sabha member is elected is called a:
solution: The area from which a Lok Sabha member is elected is a CONSTITUENCY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The electronic device used to cast votes in Indian elections is the:
solution: Votes are cast using the EVM (ELECTRONIC VOTING MACHINE). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The minimum age to vote in Indian elections is:
solution: The MINIMUM VOTING AGE is 18 YEARS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha is:
solution: The minimum age to become a LOK SABHA member is 25 YEARS (30 for Rajya Sabha). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Prime Minister is usually the leader of the:
options: Majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha
solution: The PRIME MINISTER is usually the LEADER of the MAJORITY party or coalition in the LOK SABHA. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The President of India is the:
solution: The PRESIDENT is the HEAD of STATE (constitutional head), while the PM is head of government. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The principle of 'collective responsibility' means that if a no-confidence motion passes:
options: The entire Council of Ministers must resign, not just one minister
solution: COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY means the ENTIRE Council of Ministers must RESIGN if a no-confidence motion passes. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A situation where no single party wins a clear majority in the Lok Sabha is called a:
solution: When no single party wins a clear majority, it results in a HUNG PARLIAMENT, often leading to coalitions. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Besides making laws, Parliament also performs the function of:
options: Controlling, guiding and informing the government
solution: Beyond LAW-MAKING, Parliament CONTROLS, GUIDES, and INFORMS the government (and the public). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Parliament controls the government's finances through the:
solution: Parliament controls FINANCES through the BUDGET — approving TAXES and SPENDING. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Opposition plays an important role by:
options: Criticising government policies and offering alternatives
solution: The OPPOSITION CRITICISES government policies and offers ALTERNATIVES, holding the government accountable. So option 1 is correct.

stem: India's electoral system for the Lok Sabha uses the ______ method.
solution: The LOK SABHA uses the FIRST-PAST-THE-POST method (the candidate with the most votes wins). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): Parliament represents the will of the people. Reason (R): Its members are chosen by the people through elections. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — Parliament represents the people's will. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: its members are CHOSEN by the PEOPLE through ELECTIONS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The two Houses of the Indian Parliament reflect the principle of:
solution: Having TWO Houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) reflects BICAMERALISM. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Lok Sabha — 5-year term 2. Rajya Sabha — permanent House 3. Speaker — presides over Lok Sabha. How many are correctly matched?
solution: ALL THREE match: LOK SABHA → 5-year term; RAJYA SABHA → permanent House; SPEAKER → presides over Lok Sabha. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'legislature' refers to the organ of government that:
solution: The LEGISLATURE is the organ that MAKES LAWS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A person who is a minister must usually be a member of:
options: One of the two Houses of Parliament
solution: A MINISTER must usually be a MEMBER of one of the two HOUSES of Parliament (or become one within six months). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The minimum number of members required to be present for the House to conduct business is called the:
solution: The minimum members required for the House to function is the QUORUM. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which House can be dissolved before its term ends?
solution: The LOK SABHA can be DISSOLVED before its term ends; the Rajya Sabha is a permanent House. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A representative democracy differs from a direct democracy in that people:
options: Elect representatives to make decisions on their behalf
solution: In a REPRESENTATIVE democracy, people ELECT REPRESENTATIVES to decide on their behalf. So option 1 is correct.

stem: By debating a bill in Parliament, MPs ensure that:
options: Different views are heard and the law is examined before it is passed
solution: DEBATING a bill ensures DIFFERENT VIEWS are HEARD and the law is EXAMINED before passage. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is an example of Parliament controlling the executive?
options: Passing a no-confidence motion or questioning ministers
solution: Parliament CONTROLS the executive by, e.g., passing a NO-CONFIDENCE MOTION or QUESTIONING ministers. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Lok Sabha currently has how many elected members (approximately)?
solution: The LOK SABHA currently has 543 ELECTED members. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The person elected from a constituency to the Lok Sabha is called a:
solution: A person elected to the Lok Sabha is a MEMBER of PARLIAMENT (MP). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The largest party (or alliance) that is not in government is recognised as the:
solution: The largest party NOT in government is the OFFICIAL OPPOSITION, whose leader is the Leader of the Opposition. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of 'Parliament and the Making of Laws' is that:
options: In a democracy, elected representatives in Parliament make laws and govern on behalf of the people
Laws are made by one ruler
The people have no role in law-making
solution: The chapter explains how Parliament, made up of the people's elected representatives, makes laws and governs in the name of the people.
